book.wakingworld.almanac.title: The Waker's Almanac
almanac.wakingworld.welcome.title: The Waker's Almanac
almanac.wakingworld.welcome.1: A short account of the sleeping giants, the places they were laid down, and what is asked of anyone who would wake one. Compiled from the letters of those who went before, and finished by those who came back.
almanac.wakingworld.welcome.2: The short of it: find a Dead Letter in a ruin and follow where it points. In the vaults under the fallen towers take the coal, the rune and the horn. Carry them to a shrine, lay them on its altar, and sound the horn. Then run. What it leaves behind is worth it.
almanac.wakingworld.welcome.3: The tabs down the side of this book take you to each part of the story. Where an item is spoken of, its picture is shown - hold the mouse over it to see its name.
almanac.wakingworld.advice.title: A Word of Advice
almanac.wakingworld.advice.1: The altar tells you what it wants; the letters tell you where. Take the Horn everywhere.
almanac.wakingworld.advice.2: Fight with the ground under you, not the giant. Break the lights. If it reaches for you, be somewhere else - or have wings, or water.
almanac.wakingworld.advice.3: And when it is over and the valley is a ruin, remember the Hourglass. The land forgives those who put it back.
almanac.wakingworld.sleepers.title: The Sleepers
almanac.wakingworld.sleepers.1: The hills are not all hills. Long ago the people of this land built giants out of the land itself - stone, earth, sand, ice, sea-stone and the living moss - and when the giants were no longer needed they were laid down and became the land again.
almanac.wakingworld.sleepers.2: They are still there. They are asleep, not dead. Every so often one of them turns over. Six kinds are known, each with its sigil and its rune:
almanac.wakingworld.sleepers.3: And there is talk of a seventh, in a place where the sun does not rise. Those who wrote of it did not write much.
almanac.wakingworld.kind.stone: Stone - grey rock, the oldest kind.
almanac.wakingworld.kind.stone.where: Under rings of standing stones in the hills and meadows.
almanac.wakingworld.kind.earth.where: Under the green barrows of the plains and woods.
almanac.wakingworld.kind.sandstone: Sand - sandstone, gold in the joints.
almanac.wakingworld.kind.sandstone.where: Under tombs half swallowed by the desert.
almanac.wakingworld.kind.ice: Ice - blue as the deep of a glacier.
almanac.wakingworld.kind.prismarine: The Sea - sea-stone with lanterns for eyes.
almanac.wakingworld.kind.prismarine.wher: Under sunken halls on the ocean floor.
almanac.wakingworld.kind.moss: The Grove - moss, flowers and antlers.
almanac.wakingworld.kind.moss.where: Under temples the jungle and the dark woods took back.
almanac.wakingworld.shrines.title: Shrines and Altars
almanac.wakingworld.shrines.1: Every sleeper has a shrine over it, and at the heart of every shrine an altar. You will know a shrine by its shape: a ring of standing stones, a green mound with a stone door, a tomb in the dunes, a cairn of ice, a hall under the sea, a temple under the moss.
almanac.wakingworld.shrines.altar: The Altar of the Sleeper. Right-click with an offering to lay it down; an empty hand takes the last one back.
almanac.wakingworld.shrines.2: The altar knows what lies beneath: lay a thing on it and it tells you whether it wanted that, and what it still lacks. Watch the lights around it - they wake as the offerings are laid.
almanac.wakingworld.shrines.3: It will not take an offering meant for another kind. A giant of the sea cannot be called up from a barrow, nor a giant of stone from under the ice. The altar's kind is the shrine's kind, and that is fixed.
almanac.wakingworld.shrines.4: Nothing is lost on an altar: break it or take the offerings back and they are yours again. The rite itself burns them.
almanac.wakingworld.rite.title: The Rite of Waking
almanac.wakingworld.rite.1: Three things, always. The first two are the same for every kind; the third is a gift of the land itself and differs from kind to kind - the Dead Letters know it, and so does the altar.
almanac.wakingworld.rite.ember: A coal that never went out. Every rite burns one. Only the vaults have them.
almanac.wakingworld.rite.runes: A rune cut for that kind of altar - one kind of rune for each kind of sleeper. From the vaults.
almanac.wakingworld.rite.2: The gift: something the land gives freely to those who look - the letters name it for each place.
almanac.wakingworld.rite.horn: The Horn of Waking. Hold right-click over an altar whose offerings are all laid down, and the rite begins.
almanac.wakingworld.rite.3: The ceremony takes a little while and is not quiet. Stones light, the ground breathes, the sky takes notice. Stand back.
almanac.wakingworld.rite.4: The giant rises beyond the altar, facing away from whoever blew the horn. It is never pleased to be woken.
almanac.wakingworld.vaults.title: The Vaults
almanac.wakingworld.vaults.1: The coals, the runes and the horns were laid up against the day they would be needed, in vaults dug under watchtowers. The towers have fallen; the vaults have not.
almanac.wakingworld.vaults.2: Look for a round stump of a tower on level ground with a shaft in its middle and a ladder going down. Below: a pillared hall, four rooms off it, and a crypt under the hall reached through a hole in the floor.
almanac.wakingworld.vaults.stores: The rooms hold the common stores; the crypt the rare - the horn is more often found below.
almanac.wakingworld.vaults.3: The old keepers set guards of stone down there. They are patient, and slow, and very hard - arrows only make them laugh, if they laugh. Take the rooms one at a time and never fight in the hall.
almanac.wakingworld.vaults.4: Bring light; the lanterns down there are the blue kind and do not warm you.
almanac.wakingworld.letters.title: The Dead Letters
almanac.wakingworld.letters.1: The people who lived here left in a hurry, and they left their letters behind - in cottages, in camps, at the bottom of wells, in the vaults. Read them.
almanac.wakingworld.letters.letter: A Dead Letter. Blank until it is carried; then the ink comes up, written for the place it was found in.
almanac.wakingworld.letters.2: Each one points the way to the nearest shrine or vault - or to one of the drowned cisterns and ember forges, or, now and then, to the one walled town where people still live and a king still sits - with directions and a surveyor's mark, and says in its writer's own words what that place wants. Unfold it and a compass on the page swings towards the place from wherever you stand. Follow the letters and they will take you the whole way.
almanac.wakingworld.ruins.title: The Ruins
almanac.wakingworld.ruins.1: Cottages with the roof fallen in. Watchtowers with the top come down. Wells, and what was dropped into them. Graveyards, and what was buried under them. Camps left with the fire still laid.
almanac.wakingworld.ruins.2: Whole hamlets, empty, the doors open. The land is full of them. Every one has a story, and most have a chest. Not every wall has fallen, though: far apart stand walled towns with a king in each, guards on the towers and a market in the square, where a surveyor will draw you a map to the shrines, the vaults and the next town. Be a guest there, not a thief.
almanac.wakingworld.fight.title: When It Rises
almanac.wakingworld.fight.1: A woken giant is not gentle. It walks through the wood and the wood is kindling; it tears up the ground and throws it; it will pick you up if you let it, and throw you too.
almanac.wakingworld.fight.2: Look for the lights in its body - the cores. Strike them, with a blade up close or anything that flies, and the giant weakens. It cannot be brought down while more than two still burn. Its bar tells you how many.
almanac.wakingworld.fight.hammer: The Colossus Hammer, forged around a Heart: right-click on the ground to slam, right-click in the air to dive. A giant feels this one.
almanac.wakingworld.fight.3: Keep moving. Jump the ground-waves. A grab is answered with wings or water. Watch its stance - each kind has its own tricks, and it gets angrier the more it is hurt.
almanac.wakingworld.fight.4: The bigger the giant, the longer the fall - and the bigger what it leaves.
almanac.wakingworld.spoils.title: What It Leaves
almanac.wakingworld.spoils.1: A giant that falls leaves a heap of its own stuff where it lay, and in the heap:
almanac.wakingworld.spoils.heart: Its Heart - warm for a long while. The stuff hammers and hourglasses are made of.
almanac.wakingworld.spoils.sigils: A Sigil of its kind. Six kinds, six sigils.
almanac.wakingworld.spoils.forged: Forged from a Heart: the Hammer, and the Hourglass of Restoration.
almanac.wakingworld.spoils.2: Turn the Hourglass over the ruin of a fight that is over, and the land comes back as it was. Every block. One use.
almanac.wakingworld.key.title: The Seven Sigils
almanac.wakingworld.key.1: Gather all six sigils and a Heart and forge them together, and you hold a key. It opens no door - and it turns nothing alone.
almanac.wakingworld.key.key: The Key of the Titan. It wants the great altar in the place where the sun does not rise, the seventh sigil beside it, the egg the dragon left, the six lesser altars round it burning - and the horn.
almanac.wakingworld.key.2: Those who wrote of that place did not write much more, except that what sleeps there makes the others look like children - and that it gives its heart to whoever brings it down.

wakingworld.configuration.title: The Waking World
wakingworld.configuration.colossi.toolti: The giants, their craters and their collapse.
wakingworld.configuration.letters.toolti: The letters and the AI that writes them.
Stomps, slams, landings and thrown boulders tear craters into the ground and fling the blocks around. Off: only particles, the world stays as it was.
wakingworld.configuration.trample.toolti: A walking colossus breaks through trees, plants, snow and loose ground instead of walking around them.
wakingworld.configuration.craterScale.to: Multiplier on crater sizes (0.25 = small dents, 1 = default, 2 = mountains fall).
wakingworld.configuration.maxFlyingBlock: Upper bound on falling-block entities one impact may spawn (performance).
wakingworld.configuration.collapseBlocks: How many blocks of a dying colossus come down as real falling blocks (the rest is dust). Performance.
wakingworld.configuration.deathMound.too: A dead colossus leaves a mound of its own blocks where it fell (its rubble lands on top of it).
Let Gemini write the Dead Letters for your world (needs an API key). Off or without a key: the built-in letters.
wakingworld.configuration.geminiApiKey.t: Your Google AI Studio API key (aistudio.google.com/apikey). Stays on this computer / server; never shown to other players.
wakingworld.configuration.geminiModel.to: The Gemini model that writes the letters.
wakingworld.configuration.letterLanguage: The language the AI writes the letters in (item names stay English).
wakingworld.configuration.cameraShake.to: How much the camera shakes when a colossus stomps, lands or walks nearby (0 = off, 1 = default, 2 = double).
wakingworld.configuration.bossMusic.tool: Play the colossus battle themes (awakening, one theme per kind, victory). Uses the Music volume slider.
wakingworld.configuration.riteCostMultip: Multiplies every offering count (0.5 = half price, 2 = double); each offering still needs at least one.
wakingworld.configuration.riteEmbers.too: Sleeper's Embers a shrine's altar wants.
wakingworld.configuration.riteRunes.tool: Runes of the shrine's own kind its altar wants.
wakingworld.configuration.riteGiftMultip: Multiplies the land's gift (amethyst, rooted dirt, gold, blue ice, prismarine crystals, glow berries); the defaults are 4 or 8.
wakingworld.configuration.lesserAltarRun: Runes of its land each of the six lesser altars round the Titan's wants. 0: the lesser altars are not part of the rite.
wakingworld.configuration.titanNeedsSigi: The Titan's altar wants the Void Sigil out of a reliquary besides the Key.
The Titan's altar wants the Dragon Egg besides the Key; it is given back when the Titan falls.
wakingworld.configuration.dragonEggIndes: A dropped Dragon Egg cannot burn, blow up or despawn, and one that falls into the void is set back on its island. The Titan's rite needs the egg.
wakingworld.configuration.dragonEggEvery: Every Ender Dragon that dies leaves an egg on the podium if none lies there - not only the first, as in vanilla - so a lost egg can be replaced.
entity.wakingworld.guard.say.1: Move along. The walls watch themselves, but I watch the road.
entity.wakingworld.guard.say.2: Keep your hands off the treasury and we will get along fine.
entity.wakingworld.guard.say.3: Quiet night. Too quiet - the ground has not shaken in a week.
entity.wakingworld.guard.say.4: The king sees anyone who climbs the steps. Mind your manners in the hall.
entity.wakingworld.townsfolk.refuse: The kingdom does not trade with you.
entity.wakingworld.king.angry: The king of %s will not speak with you. Not after what you did.
entity.wakingworld.king.permit: The king weighs the heart in his hands. "Very well. The treasury of %s is open to you - take what you need and leave me the crown."
kingdom.wakingworld.title: Kingdom of %s
kingdom.wakingworld.angry.guard: You struck a guard of %s. The kingdom is angry with you - its guards will hunt you for a day.
kingdom.wakingworld.angry.townsfolk: You hurt one of the people of %s. The kingdom is angry with you - the guards are coming.
kingdom.wakingworld.angry.king: You raised a hand against the king of %s! The whole kingdom turns on you.
kingdom.wakingworld.angry.king_dead: %s will not forget the death of its king for a long time.
kingdom.wakingworld.angry.treasury: Thief! The treasury of %s is warded - every guard in the kingdom knows your face now.
kingdom.wakingworld.king_dead: The king of %s is dead. The bells toll across the kingdom - the council will crown a successor.
letter.wakingworld.voice.making: the voice is still being made...
item.wakingworld.dead_letter.voice_pendi: The letter's voice is still being made - a moment.

Gemini reads every new Dead Letter aloud in its writer's voice (needs the API key). A free key allows a handful a day.
wakingworld.configuration.voiceModel.too: The Gemini text-to-speech model for the letters' voices.
wakingworld.configuration.readLettersAlo: A letter with a voice reads itself when opened and marks the words as they are read; the speaker on the letter plays, pauses and stops it either way. Voice/Speech volume.
king.wakingworld.greeting.1: Come closer, traveller. Few climb the steps to this hall who do not want something. Ask, then.
king.wakingworld.greeting.2: A stranger under my roof. The road has been kind to you, I hope - it is seldom kind to anyone these days.
king.wakingworld.greeting.3: You have the look of someone who has heard the ground move. Sit, if you like. The throne is the only chair, so you will have to stand.
king.wakingworld.kingdom.1: This kingdom was raised on the bones of an older town - the one the Dead Letters speak of. My grandfather's grandfather walled it when the giants first stirred. We keep the walls; the giants keep their sleep. That is the bargain.
king.wakingworld.kingdom.2: Trade with my people, walk my roads, drink from my fountain. Draw steel on a guard and every bow on the wall knows your face. Rob my treasury, and the whole kingdom does.
king.wakingworld.kingdom.3: The surveyor by the market sells maps to the old places, if you have emeralds and a compass. The relic-monger sells what the rites need, at a price I would not pay.
king.wakingworld.sleepers.1: Six kinds of them sleep under this land - stone, earth, sand, ice, the sea's own, and the green one under the moss. Each lies beneath a shrine of its kind, and each shrine keeps an altar with a heart in it.
king.wakingworld.sleepers.2: They are not evil. They are old, and a mountain that wakes does not look where it puts its feet. The letters call them sleepers. My people call them the reasons for the wall.
king.wakingworld.sleepers.3: If you mean to wake one, do it far from my fields. And bring the hammer. Everyone who came back had the hammer.
king.wakingworld.letters.1: The Dead Letters were written by the people who lived here before the walls: farmers, pilgrims, a scribe or two. They knew where the sleepers lay and wrote it down for whoever came after.
king.wakingworld.letters.2: My scribes have copied every one we could find. The originals are mostly in the ruins now - the buildings and the letters both. Read one and it will point you the way; the paper remembers even when the hand that wrote it is dust.
king.wakingworld.vaults.1: Under the hills there are vaults older than the shrines. Sealed doors, thralls of stone that do not tire, traps that still work after all these years.
king.wakingworld.vaults.2: Whoever built them kept what the rites need: the embers, the runes. Take what you find - but the vaults keep their doors shut for a reason, and the thralls do not care whose crown you serve.
king.wakingworld.titan.1: There is a seventh. It does not sleep under this land - it sleeps under no land at all, in the End, in an arena of black stone that the void itself laps against.
king.wakingworld.titan.2: The Key to it lies in the vaults, if you are stubborn enough to find it. But the Key alone will not turn. The arena wants another thing, kept in the void's own reliquary out among the far islands. I would not go looking. You will.
king.wakingworld.titan.3: Whoever puts it down keeps its heart. Eat that heart and it becomes part of you - for good, they say. Nothing else in this world stays.
king.wakingworld.treasury.1: What lies beneath this floor is mine, and my guards agree with me. Open a chest down there without my leave and you will hear how much they agree.
king.wakingworld.treasury.2: Bring me a Colossus Heart - a whole one, from a giant you put down yourself - and lay it in my hands. Then we will talk about what is below.
king.wakingworld.treasury.permitted: You have my leave. The trapdoor by the north-west pillar, the ladder, the iron door. Take what you need below and leave me the crown.
king.wakingworld.news.woken: They tell me a %s was woken %s to the %s, %s.
king.wakingworld.news.slain: A %s was put down %s to the %s, %s. Good riddance, or a pity - I never know which.
king.wakingworld.news.rite: A rite was sung at the %s %s to the %s, %s. The ground has not stopped humming since.
king.wakingworld.news.none: Nothing stirs that I have heard of. The scouts are bored and the farmers are glad. Long may it last.
king.wakingworld.news.end: That is all the road has brought me lately.
item.wakingworld.void_sigil.tooltip: The seventh sigil. No colossus carries it; the reliquaries of the End do. The Key of the Titan turns nothing without it and the dragon's egg.
almanac.wakingworld.key.sigil: The Void Sigil. No sleeper carries it. Out among the far islands of the End stand reliquaries, spires open to the void down their middles; the sigil waits at the top of each, behind whatever the void keeps there.
almanac.wakingworld.key.egg: The Dragon Egg. The End keeps one; the altar will not take the key without it. The Titan leaves it where it falls, cold again, for the next time - and should it ever be lost, the dragon, slain again, leaves another.
almanac.wakingworld.key.runes: The six lesser altars, on a ring round the great one, one for each land. Each wants the runes of its kind - two, unless the server's config says otherwise; the rune that woke that land's sleeper - and burns when it has them. The great altar hears no horn until all six burn; the rite takes the runes.
almanac.wakingworld.key.gate: When the Titan falls, the arena raises a gate at its southern rim: an arch of the End's own stone with the void hanging in it. Step through and you are home - in your bed, or where you first woke. The gate stands until the next rite, which takes it down; no hourglass touches it.
king.wakingworld.greeting.new: A week ago I kept a stall in the market; now I keep a kingdom. The old king's crown is heavier than it looks. Ask, and I will answer as he would have.
kingdom.wakingworld.new_king: %s has been crowned in %s. Long live the king!
almanac.wakingworld.vaults.5: Two other places keep the same things. Under a mossy pump house by the water, a flooded cistern kept by drowned who never let go of their tridents - the rune of the sea is there. Under a roofless smithy in the dry lands, with a chimney that smokes on its own, a forge that never went cold, kept by the burnt dead - the runes of stone and sand are there, and water is your friend.
trade.wakingworld.title.smith: Iron, mail and a good edge
trade.wakingworld.about.surveyor: "Walked to every shrine on these maps myself. Most of them twice; the first time I ran."
trade.wakingworld.about.relic_monger: "All of it came out of a vault with someone who did not come back to sell it."
trade.wakingworld.about.smith: "The guards' mail is mine. What the giants wear I have tried to work. It works you."
trade.wakingworld.about.provisioner: "Take bread. Whatever you mean to wake, you will want to have eaten first."
trade.wakingworld.about.chandler: "A lantern is the difference between a vault and a grave. Buy two."
trade.wakingworld.about.scribe: "The letters come to me first. I copy what I can read and sell what I cannot."
